title: Durable Repository Orientation Graph and Incremental Semantic Index

preflight.note: Created after the Repository Orientation Graph concept was discussed and after H15/S8 orientation-cost metrics were pre-registered, but before any ROG implementation, durable graph format, language adapter, adoption integration, cache, Workbench extension, or graph-enabled benchmark run begins. The work item follows a Sol High architecture review of the live WI054/WI056 Rust graph and engine boundaries.

acceptance_criteria.text: Record a durable architecture decision before implementation makes a persistent graph format canonical. The decision defines the graph's repository path, schema/version contract, sharding/canonical serialization, source-projection fingerprint, enablement semantics, local-cache boundary, migration/backfill behavior, and the fact that the graph is derived rather than a new source of truth.

Extend the canonical WI054 Rust graph/query authority instead of creating a second competing graph implementation. Existing governance nodes and relationships remain canonical for governance, while repository-orientation layers add physical, semantic, build/test/operational relationships and deterministic cross-layer links.

Define a typed multilayer node model covering at minimum repository, directory, file, workspace/package/crate/module, configuration/build/test/runtime surfaces, selected language symbols, and the existing RepoPact governance node classes. Node identity is deterministic and repository-relative; line numbers alone are not primary symbol identity.

Define an explicit edge taxonomy for physical containment, definitions/imports/exports, dependencies/reverse dependencies, selected references/calls/implementation relations where supported, build/package/test/runtime relations, and governance applicability. Unsupported or low-certainty relationships are not presented as exact facts.

Every durable graph relationship carries enough explanation metadata to identify its relation kind, source path/location where available, derivation mechanism, provenance/certainty class, and graph schema/generator context. Clients can explain why an edge exists without relying on an opaque model score.

Define and enforce derivation classes that distinguish canonical RepoPact-record relationships, deterministic parser relationships, manifest/build-system relationships, and any future heuristic/inferred relationships. LLM or heuristic output is never silently promoted to concrete graph authority.

Implement a deterministic portable durable graph representation suitable for Git versioning, clean-clone loading, corruption detection, and canonical rebuild. The representation includes a manifest plus stable partitioning/sharding of graph data so unrelated source changes do not rewrite the entire graph unnecessarily.

Do not make a committed SQLite, sled, RocksDB, or other opaque binary database the sole durable graph representation. A local acceleration database is permitted only as a disposable, reconstructable cache whose deletion loses no repository-authoritative state.

Define a canonical source projection and fingerprint that excludes the graph's own derived files and explicitly excluded cache/generated paths, avoids circular self-hashing, and uses stable path/content or Git object identities where available. Graph freshness can be verified without blindly reparsing every source file.

Expose explicit graph freshness/capability states including at least fresh, working-overlay or dirty-aware, partial, stale, unsupported, and corrupt (exact naming may differ). No supported client may silently present stale or partial graph output as a current complete repository map.

Canonical full graph rebuilds from the same source projection and graph-schema version are deterministic and byte-equivalent after documented normalization across repeated runs and supported platforms. Nondeterministic timestamps or traversal order may not poison the fixpoint.

Incremental graph update is proven equivalent to a clean full rebuild for every supported change class: after canonical normalization, G_incremental(s0->s1) equals G_full(s1). Tests cover additions, edits, deletes, renames/moves where supported, manifest changes, relationship changes, and parser-failure recovery.

Integrate with RepositorySession/snapshot and the existing watcher model so uncommitted working-tree changes can invalidate or update a local graph overlay without rewriting the durable baseline on every keystroke. Query results disclose when dirty working-tree state contributes to the answer.

Integrate graph bootstrap with brownfield adoption after governance discovery/import: repository discovery -> governance adoption -> orientation discovery -> graph build -> graph validation/materialization -> orientation summary -> final validation. Graph generation does not fabricate governance facts to make adoption pass.

Provide an explicit deterministic backfill path for already-governed repositories, such as `repopact graph build` plus status/verify operations and, only if separately justified, doctor migration. Existing adopters are not silently forced to accept a large persistent artifact without a versioned capability contract.

Prove the clean-clone success path: a fresh client can clone a graph-enabled repository, verify graph schema/fingerprint, load the durable graph or rebuild a local acceleration cache, and answer bounded orientation queries without first performing a full repository text search or reparsing the entire repository.

Define a language-neutral adapter interface for semantic extraction. Evaluate Tree-sitter or an equivalent incremental parser substrate and record the selected approach based on determinism, incremental behavior, portability, parse safety, language coverage, packaging cost, and integration with the Rust core.

Initial semantic coverage is sufficient to orient RepoPact itself and includes at least Rust, Python, and TypeScript/JavaScript source structure plus relevant JSON/TOML/YAML/Markdown and manifest metadata. Coverage is reported per language and relation; support for a language does not falsely imply a complete call graph.

Add deterministic build/package/test/operational adapters where repository metadata supports them, including at least Cargo workspace/dependency metadata, Python package/project metadata, JavaScript/TypeScript package and tsconfig/workspace metadata, CI workflow references, test targets/fixtures, generated boundaries, installer/package surfaces, and runtime/application entry points used by RepoPact.

Coverage gaps are first-class graph output. Unsupported languages, parser failures, excluded trees, and relationships unavailable at the chosen extraction tier are reported explicitly. Partial coverage is never represented as complete repository understanding.

Implement safe repository-boundary and exclusion behavior: do not follow symlinks outside the repository by default, do not index `.git` internals as source, honor RepoPact/graph exclusions, classify submodules or nested repos, bound vendor/generated/dependency trees, avoid common build/cache/venv/node_modules/target outputs by default, and do not ingest ignored secret files merely because they exist locally.

Language adapters are resource-bounded and failure-isolated for malformed or adversarial repository content. Define and test file-size/binary/minified/generated policies, cancellation or timeout behavior, recursion/depth bounds where applicable, malformed syntax handling, path normalization, parser memory behavior, and recovery after a failed region parse.

Expose a typed agent/query API from the canonical Rust engine covering graph status, target resolution, context/orientation, neighbors, path, dependencies, reverse dependencies, impact, tests, governance, and other narrowly justified operations. Results include stable IDs, relation kinds, source references, freshness, and provenance/derivation metadata.

Implement a bounded orientation query for a work item, path, package, module, type, or symbol that can return identity, containment, direct dependencies/dependents, relevant tests, build/runtime/package surfaces, applicable RepoPact governance, coverage/freshness warnings, and a small source-backed list of files or nodes to inspect first. Facts are distinguished from heuristic recommendations.

Graph query outputs support explicit bounds such as maximum nodes/edges, depth, relation filters, pagination/cursors, output byte/token budget, and source-reference-only modes. Truncation is explicit and resumable rather than silently dropping graph neighborhoods.

Add practical public CLI and versioned engine-protocol operations for graph build/status/verify plus orientation/context/impact/tests/governance queries. Python compatibility clients, Workbench, agents, and future clients use typed protocol results rather than scraping presentation strings.

Extend the Workbench's existing graph surface into an operator-oriented repository map with node resolution/search, layer/relation filters, bounded neighborhood drill-in, source navigation, impact/test/governance views, freshness/coverage state, and authorized rebuild/verify controls. A force-directed visual canvas is optional and is not the primary acceptance criterion.

Workbench graph behavior remains usable across wide and compact form factors without making essential operations depend on hover or right-click. Durable graph semantics are path-normalized and portable across Windows/Linux/macOS; mobile capability handling composes with WI061 rather than assuming unrestricted filesystem or system-Git access.

Define branch/merge/conflict behavior for derived graph files. Source merge resolution remains authoritative; graph conflicts can be repaired by deterministic regeneration; the sharding strategy minimizes unrelated churn; no workflow requires humans to hand-merge graph semantics that can be rederived from source.

Version the durable graph schema and define compatibility/migration behavior. Unknown major graph versions fail or report unsupported rather than being interpreted optimistically. Graph format evolution is separable from unrelated RepoPact spec changes where practical.

Add graph validation/conformance coverage for manifest/shard schema, hashes, duplicate node IDs, dangling edges, canonical sort/serialization, source-fingerprint match, self-exclusion, deterministic rebuild, incremental/full equivalence, clean clone, corruption, staleness, partial coverage, unsupported language behavior, path normalization, symlink/nested-repo boundaries, and graph-disabled compatibility.

Produce performance and storage evidence on RepoPact plus documented larger fixtures: full build time, incremental update time by change class, peak memory, durable graph size, local-cache size, node/edge counts, clean-clone verification/load time, representative query latency, parser coverage, graph/source size ratio, and branch/merge rebuild cost. Any product limit is justified by measurements rather than intuition.

Before any graph-enabled comparative result is collected, append a dated amendment to `research/benchmark-protocol.md` defining the S8 R1 graph-enabled condition without rewriting existing B0/R0 conditions, tasks, or metrics. The amendment is committed before exploratory R1 runs that could influence the evaluation contract.

Evaluate R1 against the already-registered S8 correctness and orientation-cost measures, including governance/violation recovery, false-clean rate, authority-state error, orientation time, tokens, tool calls, file reads, repository-wide grep/search operations, bytes read, and human interventions. Reduced search with degraded correctness is not accepted as a win.

Document adoption, enable/disable, rebuild, verification, freshness, graph-query, unsupported-language, privacy/exclusion, cache, and troubleshooting workflows for both human operators and agents. Documentation distinguishes durable graph facts from heuristics and from authoritative source/governance records.

The deterministic ROG core requires no LLM, embedding/vector database, cloud indexing service, or external provider. Any future assisted semantic enrichment is proposal/inferred only, is clearly provenance-typed, and cannot silently become governance or mutation authority.

Graph queries and Workbench views do not bypass WI054 typed mutation plan/apply, frozen-surface approval, WI050 admission/enforcement, Tauri IPC/capability boundaries, evidence/provenance rules, or repository path restrictions. Graph impact data may inform a mutation plan but never authorizes it.

Closeout evidence enumerates the exact durable format, paths, schema, fingerprint, node/edge classes, language/relation coverage, query surface, cache behavior, Workbench surface, unsupported capabilities, parser/resource limits, cross-platform normalization, performance/storage results, security/adversarial tests, and remaining future work, with links to executable evidence rather than prose-only claims.

Define a backward-compatible capability contract: repositories without the ROG or with it explicitly disabled remain valid RepoPact repositories unless a later governed version decision changes that rule; when the ROG capability is declared enabled, its durable manifest/freshness/validation requirements become binding and may not silently degrade to an absent graph.

Prove by API design and tests that graph data itself cannot grant ownership, approval, lifecycle authority, criterion waiver, frozen-surface acknowledgement, invariant mutation, or evidence truth. Those authorities continue to derive from their existing RepoPact source records and governed mutation/admission paths.
